summary: Babylon is fallen, is fallen!—Other nations also are destroyed.
meta_description: Babylon is fallen, is fallen!—Other nations also are destroyed.

footnotes.note1_a: IE a message or prophecy of doom to Babylon.
footnotes.note2_b: This prophecy was fulfilled in 538 B.C., about 200 years after Isaiah lived.
footnotes.note3_a: IE Isaiah was astonished at the cataclysmic scene he saw in vision, even though an enemy was the nation destroyed.
footnotes.note10_a: HEB O my threshed one and son of my threshing floor. (The prophet thus addressed the Israelites who will survive Babylon’s downfall.)
footnotes.note11_a: IE a message of doom to the Edomites.
footnotes.note11_c: IE How much is spent? How long will darkness (i.e., oppression) last?
footnotes.note12_a: IE The end of Babylonian captivity approaches, but another oppressor follows; inquire again later.
footnotes.note13_a: Arabian caravans and camps would also suffer disruption and oppression by the Babylonian conquest (vv. 13–17).
